 Insurer combines entertainment and sports for healthier lifestyles
 AIA Life Korea hosts its “K-Pop Together, Give Together” concert at KINTEX near Seoul on Oct. 24, bringing together roughly 7,000 from Korea and across Asia. [Photo courtesy of AIA Life Korea] 
 A IA Life Korea announced on Nov. 12 that the financial firm was expanding its wellness initiatives through K-pop concerts, running events, and charitable activities.
 The insurer noted that such an initiative came as the concept of healthy living increasingly extends beyond physical fitness to mental well-being and social connections.
 AIA Life Korea said that its programs reflect a broader shift toward wellness designed to improve quality of life through enjoyable everyday experiences rather than focus solely on disease prevention and treatment.
 Running, for example, has evolved from an individual fitness activity into a social experience in which participants pursue common goals and celebrate achievements together, according to the company.
 Cultural activities, including concerts and exhibitions, are also attracting attention as ways to relieve stress, improve emotional well-being, and strengthen interpersonal relationships.
 Against this backdrop, insurers are increasingly exploring ways to support customers’ well-being beyond traditional financial protection against illness and accidents, AIA Life Korea said.
 The Seoul-based outfit, part of the Hong Kong-based AIA Group , stated that it has been developing programs that combine physical activity, cultural experiences, and community engagement.
 The insurer recently introduced “AIA WE,” short for AIA Wellness & Entertainment, building on its existing customer engagement initiative, AIA-Only Experience.
 The program aims to encourage healthier lifestyles through enjoyable sports and cultural activities while creating opportunities for participants to connect with one another.
 As part of the initiative, AIA Life Korea hosted the “K-Pop Together, Give Together” concert on Oct. 24, bringing together about 7,000 participants from South Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Singapore.
 Attendees included customers, employees, family members, and business partners affiliated with AIA Life Korea and AIA Premier Partners, as well as participants from the insurer’s regional network.
 The concert featured performances by popular Korean artists, including Jinusean , ITZY , J.Y. Park , Chungha , and Psy .
 AIA Life Korea also donated more than 260 million won ($200,000) to two nonprofit organizations.
 Beyond entertainment, the insurer has expanded its involvement in running events to encourage physical activity, community participation and charitable giving.
 In August, its AIA Running Story Crew participated in the 2026 Habitat 815 Run , a charity event supporting housing improvements for descendants of Korean independence activists.
 The following month, around 330 people participated in the inaugural AIA Track Day at a park in Seoul, where runners of different ages and fitness levels gathered to experience the benefits and enjoyment of running.
 On Nov. 1, AIA Life Korea also participated in the 2026 JTBC Seoul Marathon for the fourth consecutive year.
 A total of 1,100 runners representing AIA Life Korea and AIA Premier Partners took part in the event, including customers, financial planners, telemarketers, business partners, and employees.
 Under its “Run Together, Give Together” initiative , the insurer pledged to donate 100,000 won ($75) for each participating runner, raising a total of 110 million won ($83,000).
 Hwang Ji-ye , chief marketing officer of AIA Life Korea, said that the company’s wellness initiatives demonstrate how shared experiences can translate into meaningful contributions to society.
 “Seeing the songs we sang together at the concert and the joy of crossing the marathon finish line turn into acts of giving reminded us of the true meaning of wellness that AIA WE seeks to promote,” she said.
 “We will continue expanding accessible sports and cultural programs so that more people can develop healthy habits, connect with one another and experience healthier, longer, better lives.”
